investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds across all three sibling checks, causing the eval to time out before any VM was provisioned and before any required evidence could be written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds across all three sibling checks, causing the eval to time out before any VM was provisioned and before any required evidence could be written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-14T00:53–00:58Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also exhausted — no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 kata-capable nodes, and preemption is not applicable to affinity mismatches. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~146–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 kata-capable nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so the pool of schedulable nodes is structurally limited to those 2 nodes. When those 2 are full, the entire cluster is effectively unavailable for this workload.

[Possible] Preemption policy prevents recovery: the scheduler found no lower-priority pods to evict on the 2 kata-capable nodes, meaning the cluster cannot self-heal by displacing other workloads. This is consistent with 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' in failed-check.message.

[Possible] Concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are simultaneously holding VM slots on the 2 kata nodes, the resource pool could be transiently exhausted. No concurrent-run evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

[Lower confidence] A cluster scaling or node provisioning event reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before this run: no node event or scaling log evidence is present in the supplied packet.
